- Observe a[i] mod 3 pattern: a[i] = i^2 − i + 1; since i(i−1) is always even and divisible by 2, check mod 3: squares mod 3 are 0,1; compute i^2−i ≡ i(i−1) ≡ 0 mod 3 for any i, hence a[i] ≡ 1 mod 3 for all i. Therefore every element is congruent to 1 mod 3.
- A triple sum is multiple of 3 iff the sum of residues mod 3 is 0. With all residues = 1, 1+1+1 = 3 ≡ 0, so every distinct triple qualifies.
- Compute and return the number of 3-combinations from n: C(n,3) = n*(n−1)*(n−2)/6 (handle n < 3 returning 0).
